solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Peers slam old report that's recycled

indicators.note: something recycled is broken down and made into something new, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords angrily criticise an old document that has been reissued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link. The Lords Temporal are the non-bishop members of the British House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lords Temporal are the secular members of the House of Lords, all of them peers of the realm.

clue.text: Sailor introduced to African as believer in free will

indicators.note: the sailor is brought into the middle of the African, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a Liberian is a person from Liberia in West Africa
tar is an old slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman meets an African who believes in free will.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy a libertarian holds that human choices are free, not determined in advance.

clue.text: Spanish runner clutches at relationship

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tightly, so the runner wraps around the other word

parts.note: rio is Spanish for river, and a river runs

explanation.surface: A Spanish athlete grabs at something.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'runner' in crosswords is often a river; here it is the Spanish word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the quantitative relation between two amounts, such as three to one.

clue.text: Dumpy, small, unfortunate: close to collapse inside

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: the final letter is put within the word for unfortunate

parts.note: hapless means unlucky or unfortunate

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A description of someone short, stout and unlucky who is about to keel over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dumpy is squat and without elegant form, so it lacks a good figure or outline.

clue.text: Lover that was hardly hunky offers excuse

parts.note: a former lover is an ex
someone hardly hunky is not good-looking, i.e. plain

explanation.surface: A former boyfriend who was never handsome comes up with an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offers' is a link: the wordplay offers the definition. 'Excuse' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a lapse is to justify it, and explaining a mistake can account for it in the same way.

clue.text: Old man should cover chest in something warm

indicators.note: covering the chest means the old man goes around it

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Advice that Dad should wrap his chest in something cosy.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded, insulated jacket worn to keep out the cold.

clue.text: Hound someone to set situation straight?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who retrieves, or rescues, a situation

explanation.walkthrough: To 'retrieve the situation' is an idiom for putting a bad position right; the question mark flags the invented noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a gun dog that fetches game, and jokingly a person who rescues things.

clue.text: Learner driver on two wheels for convenience?

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
each O looks like a wheel

explanation.surface: A learner rides a two-wheeler because it is convenient.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'convenience' in Britain is a public toilet; the question mark flags the misleading sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Public convenience is the British euphemism for a public toilet.

clue.text: Nothing took effect in late news report

parts.note: O resembles zero, nothing
a measure bit when it started to take effect

explanation.surface: Nothing had changed by the time of the late-night bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a news report on someone recently deceased, the late person of the clue.

clue.text: Spirit level in a mine brought to one working

indicators.note: the last pieces are brought up to join what comes before
the level is placed within the mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
par means equal level, as in 'on a par'
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means working or operating, like a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A spirit level taken down a mine to someone at work there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit level' is a tool, but the clue splits it: 'Spirit' is the definition and 'level' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition is a ghost, a supernatural spirit that appears to the living.

clue.text: Gardens conveyed in painting — Appian's first

indicators.note: the word for conveyed sits within the word for painting

parts.note: painting is a form of art
bore is the past tense of bear, to carry

indicators.note: only the first letter of Appian's is used

explanation.surface: Gardens depicted in a painting, with the Appian one leading.
explanation.walkthrough: ARBORETA is the Latin plural of arboretum.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden devoted to trees, so the plural names several such gardens.

clue.text: Noble philosopher denying Trinity at the end

indicators.note: to deny something is to refuse it, so these letters are removed from the philosopher
the removal happens at the end of the philosopher's name

parts.note: Aristotle was the Greek philosopher
a trinity is a set of three, here the last three letters

explanation.surface: An aristocratic thinker who rejects the Holy Trinity in his final days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trinity' is not religious here: it just means three letters come off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristo is informal short for aristocrat, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Measure in sections bending rule time and time again

indicators.note: bending something twists it out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: rule as written, T for time twice (the physics abbreviation), and the word again, with and as a joining word

explanation.surface: Someone measuring in parts, breaking the rules repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and time again' reads as an idiom, but it yields T, T and the word AGAIN, all thrown in with RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveyors triangulate by dividing land into triangles and measuring their angles.

clue.text: Note in Rule Ten wrong about competition at court

indicators.note: the note goes in between the word for rule and ten

parts.note: a law is a rule

indicators.note: about signals the word for wrong is turned round

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A note in the tenth rule is wrong about a competition held at a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks royal or legal, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis is the formal name of the game played on a grass or hard court.

clue.text: Queen playing Free Bird in six counties?

indicators.note: the bird and anagram go inside the six counties

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is made up of six counties

indicators.note: playing a word loosely rearranges its letters

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A queen performing the song Free Bird across Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free Bird' is a Lynyrd Skynyrd song title, but here it splits into anagram fodder and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was the ancient Egyptian royal consort of Pharaoh Akhenaten.

clue.text: Ridicules flowers bought at the weekend?

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, a day at the weekend
irises are flowers

explanation.surface: Flowers someone purchased on a weekend day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bought' is a link, and the question mark flags that the phrase reads two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise is to mock using irony or exaggeration, which is a way of ridiculing.

clue.text: Wrongdoer renouncing evil — that's pointless

indicators.note: a wrongdoer who renounces evil gives it up, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a villain is a wrongdoer
ill means evil, as in 'ill will'

explanation.surface: A criminal giving up wickedness, which turns out to be futile.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain attempt is one that is futile, without result or purpose.

clue.text: Land granted that is held between two forces

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits between the two letters for forces

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force, twice
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Territory awarded and held between two armies.
explanation.definitionFit: A fief was an estate a feudal lord granted to a vassal in return for service.

clue.text: Little son carrying weight

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
something carrying weight is mattering, being important

explanation.surface: A small boy carrying something heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little son' looks like one phrase, but 'Little' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a small amount, as in a smattering of French.

clue.text: Welcome account — one saying little about India

parts.note: AC is the banking abbreviation for account

indicators.note: the word for one saying little goes around the letter for India

parts.note: a clam is a person who says little, from 'clam up'
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A warm report given by a quiet person about India.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to greet with enthusiastic praise, as a crowd hails a hero.

clue.text: One leaving whole sheep's heart in dish

indicators.note: the one leaves the word, so its letter is dropped

parts.note: entire means whole
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the heart of the word for the animal is its central letter

parts.note: taken as the word sheep

explanation.surface: A cook leaves a whole sheep's heart in a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a course served at a meal: a main course in America, a starter in Britain.

clue.text: Powerful symbol used regularly in mezangelle

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

explanation.surface: A strong emblem appears often in mezangelle, an internet poetry style.
explanation.walkthrough: Mezangelle is a hybrid poetic language devised by the net artist Mez Breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle stands for might and empire on flags and coats of arms, from Rome to the USA.

clue.text: Traveller involved primarily in china and metal

indicators.note: the traveller and letter go inside the friend

parts.note: china, from rhyming slang 'china plate' = mate, means a chum
a Rom is a Romany traveller

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A traveller deals mainly in porcelain and metal goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is not porcelain: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromium is the hard shiny element used in chrome plating and stainless steel.

clue.text: Husband to Mathilde perhaps housing old south sea islander

indicators.note: housing something means holding it inside

parts.note: mari is French for husband, and Mathilde is a French name

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's husband sheltering an elderly Pacific islander.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the Polynesian people native to New Zealand in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Instrument getting fish on line

indicators.note: the fish is placed on, following, the line

parts.note: a string is a line or cord
bass is a fish

explanation.surface: An angling tool that catches fish on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fishing tackle, but the answer is the double bass.
explanation.definitionFit: The string bass, or double bass, is the largest bowed instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Physicist at last uncovered huge gravitational force

indicators.note: only the last letter of Physicist is taken
uncovering a word removes its outer letters

parts.note: first letter of huge
last letter of huge

explanation.surface: A physicist finally discovers a huge gravitational force.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a strong pull, and gravity is a force that pulls objects together.

clue.text: Stone work filling in wall

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A stonemason's job of filling a gap in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone known for its shifting play of colours.

clue.text: Good Scottish man to avoid French island cruise?

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good
Ed is a man's name
to miss is to avoid
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: A decent Scot steering clear of a French island on a holiday cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruise' looks like a holiday, but it is the Cruise missile; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cruise is a type of low-flying weapon steered to its target, an example of the answer.
